html:
On 22 July 2011 a far-right extremist killed 77 people in Norway, with a bomb in central Oslo and a shooting at a youth camp on the island of Utøya.

The car bomb at the government offices killed eight. He then shot 69 people, most of them teenagers, at the Labour Party camp.

The killer said he was fighting multiculturalism and Muslim immigration. He was sentenced to 21 years in prison, which can be extended.

It was the deadliest day in Norway since the Second World War. The prime minister answered with a call for more democracy and openness, and crowds filled the streets with roses. The attack drew attention to far-right violence in Europe and influenced later killers. Compare the attacks in Paris in 2015.
sum: On 22 July 2011 a far-right extremist killed 77 people in Norway, with a bomb in central Oslo and a shooting at a youth camp on the island of Utøya.
